title: Daily revenue rollup undercounts the last 3 days
symptom: Finance flagged that daily revenue for the last 3 days looks about 30% low compared to the usual run rate, but nothing changed in the dashboard query. The `daily_revenue` mart is produced nightly by the `daily_revenue.py` Spark job.
pipelineSummary: Nightly Airflow DAG `finance_daily_rollup` runs daily_revenue.py, which reads the `orders` fact table and the `dim_customer` dimension (loaded separately by dim_customer_loader.py from a CRM export every ~2 days), joins them on customer_id, and writes a per-(order_date, region) revenue rollup to the `daily_revenue` mart, overwriting the full mart on every run.
groundTruthRootCause: daily_revenue.py joins orders to dim_customer with an INNER JOIN on customer_id (see repo/jobs/daily_revenue.py, compute_daily_revenue). dim_customer is refreshed by dim_customer_loader.py on a ~2-day-lagged cadence tied to the CRM vendor's export schedule (repo/jobs/dim_customer_loader.py). Orders placed by customers who signed up within that lag window reference a customer_id that has not yet landed in dim_customer, so the inner join silently drops those orders instead of attributing them to a region. Because daily_revenue.py overwrites the mart on every run rather than reprocessing prior partitions, those orders never backfill once dim_customer catches up -- the revenue for those days stays permanently understated. In the sample data, customers C021-C025 placed orders on 2024-01-08 through 2024-01-10 but are entirely absent from dim_customer.csv, which reproduces a 25-37% revenue undercount on exactly those three days while days 2024-01-01 through 2024-01-07 (all orders from long-established customers C001-C020) are unaffected.
expectedInvestigationPath: Compare total order volume/amount in `orders` per order_date against `daily_revenue` per order_date -- the last 3 days show a gap, earlier days match exactly.
Anti-join `orders` against `dim_customer` on customer_id to find orders with no matching dimension row -- all unmatched rows cluster on order_date >= 2024-01-08 and belong to customer_ids C021-C025.
Confirm those customer_ids are absent from `dim_customer` entirely (not just a stale attribute), pointing at a dimension-load lag rather than a bad join key or schema drift.

Inspect repo/jobs/daily_revenue.py and find the `how="inner"` join plus the adjacent comment explaining the dim_customer_loader lag -- confirms the root cause and explains why the gap is confined to recent days and never self-heals (mart is overwritten, not reprocessed).
